learn.hardTeach: Pliny, Letters 10.97. Trajan’s rescript: they are not to be hunted out. If they are brought and persist, they are to be punished. If they deny and worship our gods, they are to be pardoned. Christ’s name is already a public Roman problem. Trajan does not invent a secret club. He answers a governor who already heard Christians sing to Christ. Do not claim Trajan wrote a Gospel. Hold the edict: do not hunt them out.

journal.title: Do not hunt them out
journal.p: Trajan writes: do not hunt Christians out. The emperor treats Christ’s name as a public case, not a secret hunt. Pliny already heard them sing to Christ. Trajan answers with an edict, not a Gospel.
The churches already named Christ in the open. Rome had to decide what to do with that name.

He is not telling Easter. He is naming a people already known in Rome by Christ’s name. Easy does not rest on the harder Claudius / Chrestus line.

learn.hardTeach: Suetonius, Nero 16.2. Punishment was inflicted on the Christians, a class of men given to a new and mischievous superstition. That is a Roman life of Nero, not a church tract. Tacitus also names Nero’s punishment of people called Christians. Hold Nero 16.2. Claudius 25.4 (Chrestus) is a different sentence and a later fight — Easy does not rest on it. Christ is named here as the people called Christians.
